title: Broadcom vs. Marvell Technology: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: Broadcom and Marvell Technology are compared as semiconductor investments in the AI-driven data center market. Broadcom, a diversified infrastructure giant with $1.7T market cap, offers lower valuation multiples and locked-in multi-year revenue commitments from major tech companies. Marvell, a smaller pure-play data infrastructure specialist with $236B market cap, shows faster growth (42% YoY) but higher valuation and customer concentration risks. The article recommends Broadcom for its superior forward visibility and expanding AI revenue base.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy with locked-in multi-year revenue commitments from major customers (Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic), strong free cash flow ($26.9B), higher gross margins (66.54%), lower P/E ratio (45.61x), and faster AI revenue expansion on a larger base providing superior forward visibility.

Described as a strong contender with impressive 42% YoY revenue growth and Nvidia backing, but faces higher valuation multiples (P/E 88.49x), extreme customer concentration (82% from top 10 customers), lower gross margins (51.42%), and slower underlying AI business growth compared to Broadcom despite recent stock outperformance.

title: Marvell's New $18 Billion Revenue Target Could be a Game-Changer
author: Rick Orford
description: Marvell Technology has set an ambitious $18 billion fiscal 2028 revenue target, leveraging custom AI chip wins, hyperscaler partnerships, and optical connectivity opportunities. The key question for investors is whether the company's growth can accelerate fast enough to justify its current valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article highlights Marvell's ambitious $18 billion revenue target and growth opportunities in custom AI chips and optical connectivity. The company is positioned as a beneficiary of big tech designing its own AI chips. However, the sentiment is tempered by valuation concerns and the question of whether growth can justify current stock prices.

title: Does Credo's $525M-$535M Revenue Outlook Signal Further Upside?
author: Na
description: Credo Technology reported record Q1 fiscal 2027 revenues of $479M (up 115% y/y) with seven consecutive quarters of triple-digit growth, driven by AI infrastructure investments and demand for high-speed connectivity solutions. The company projects Q2 revenues of $525M-$535M and expects fiscal 2027 optical revenues to exceed $600M with a non-GAAP net margin of approximately 50%. Competitors Broadcom and Marvell Technology are also benefiting from strong AI semiconductor demand with significant revenue growth forecasts.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Record Q1 revenues with 115% y/y growth, seven consecutive quarters of triple-digit growth, strong Q2 guidance ($525M-$535M), and expectations of 85%+ fiscal 2027 revenue growth with 50% net margins demonstrate exceptional business momentum and market demand.

Fiscal 2026 AI semiconductor revenues expected to reach $58B (up 186% y/y), secured supply for $115B in fiscal 2027 revenues, and fiscal 2028 projections of $230B in AI semiconductor revenues indicate strong growth trajectory and market leadership.

Record data center revenues, fiscal 2027 revenue outlook raised to $12B (45% growth), fiscal 2028 forecast increased to $18B (50% growth), and expanding role in AI architectures through custom programs and acquisitions demonstrate strong momentum.

title: Intel vs. Marvell Technology: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: Intel and Marvell Technology represent different plays in the AI-driven semiconductor market. Intel is undergoing a major turnaround to become a foundry while maintaining CPU dominance, reporting near-breakeven results with significant ongoing capital expenditures. Marvell focuses on data center networking and posted strong 42% revenue growth with a 32.6% net margin. The article concludes Marvell is the better buy due to its growth trajectory, lower valuation multiples, and lack of business model uncertainty, while Intel faces risks from its costly restructuring and government involvement.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Intel is in the midst of a costly turnaround with massive capital expenditures for foundry buildout, reported a $267M net loss, carries negative free cash flow of $4.9B, and faces significant execution risks. The author expresses concern about the company's business model overhaul and government involvement.

Marvell demonstrated strong 42.1% revenue growth, achieved a healthy 32.6% net margin, generated positive free cash flow of $1.4B, and maintains a lower forward P/E ratio of 59.6 vs Intel's 63.7. The company is growing profitably without major business model disruption.

title: As Big Tech Designs Its Own AI Chips, the Companies Behind the Scenes Win
author: Chris Neiger
description: As major tech companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon develop custom AI processors instead of relying solely on GPUs, semiconductor designers and manufacturers are positioned to benefit significantly. Custom processors are growing 45% annually compared to 16% for GPUs, with companies like Broadcom, Marvell, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing capturing substantial market share and revenue growth.
